text: 68-year-old male. The patient reports having a fever, cough, weakness, night sweats, and poor appetite persisting for 6 months. He has lost 7.5 kg (16.5 lb) over this period. No history of breathlessness, nasal discharge, nasal obstruction, palpitations, chest pain, or digestive symptoms. Released from prison 9 months ago after a 2-year sentence.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age, significant weight loss, night sweats, and the fact that you were recently released from prison, I am concerned about an infectious etiology. Have you ever been tested for tuberculosis before, or have you had any close contacts with known cases?

text: My main symptom is Chronic cough and fever. I also have Weight loss, Night sweats, Generalized weakness, Poor appetite.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pulmonary Tuberculosis. The mention of appendicitis is incorrect given your lack of abdominal pain; your symptoms of chronic cough, fever, night sweats, and weight loss are classic for TB. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray findings.
